region: Tropical Africa, from West Africa to East Africa
description: Iroko is a durable, yellow-brown African hardwood that darkens with age and is often used as a cheaper substitute for teak. Woodworkers use it for outdoor furniture, boat work, worktops, joinery and flooring.

hazards.summary: Iroko dust is a confirmed cause of occupational asthma. In an Italian study all nine affected woodworkers had asthma reactions when challenged with iroko dust in the clinic, and a Spanish case was confirmed the same way.
The UK safety regulator names iroko as one of the woods that can rarely cause allergic alveolitis, a flu-like lung inflammation that can lead to lasting lung damage.
Dermatitis from iroko is listed by the UK safety regulator, and case reports describe allergic skin rashes from iroko dust, including on the face from airborne dust.
The UK safety regulator lists nettle rash (hives) among the reported effects of iroko.
IARC classifies all wood dust as carcinogenic to humans, mainly linked to cancers of the nasal cavity and sinuses after long-term exposure.

related_species_note: Milicia regia (also traded as iroko) is a close relative; evidence here is reported simply as iroko and may include either species. 'African teak' is a trade name only; iroko is not related to true teak.
image_prompt: Photorealistic studio photograph of a freshly planed iroko (Milicia excelsa) board, shot at a low three-quarter angle so the face grain fills most of the frame. Heartwood a yellowish to golden-brown with a slight greenish cast on the fresh surface, mid-way between yellow and teak-brown; a narrow band of pale cream sapwood clearly set apart along one edge. Interlocked grain giving a faint ribbon stripe, coarse even texture with large open pores visible as fine dark streaks, a few scattered small pale mineral deposits, and a moderate natural luster. Soft diffused daylight from upper left, gentle falloff, neutral warm-grey seamless background, shallow depth of field with the near edge tack-sharp. No text, no logos, no hands, no tools, no finish or varnish, natural unfinished wood. Wide 1200x630 composition (1.91:1) with the board centered and margin on both sides for cropping.
image_alt: Planed board of iroko with yellowish golden-brown heartwood, coarse open grain and a narrow band of pale sapwood.
notes_internal: Asthma level 1: Ricciardi-2003 (bronchial provocation positive in 9 workers; skin prick and sIgE negative, suggesting a non-IgE mechanism) and Azofra-1989 (bronchial provocation, early and late response). Pickering-1972 has no abstract; cited as supporting only. Hinnen-1995 and Stingeni-1998 are letters without abstracts; patch-test details not confirmed, so dermatitis stays at level 2 via HSE-WIS30. Unused leads: Casas-2003 (Spanish case, PMID 12605819), de las Marinas-2013 (basophil activation test, PMID 24654319), Kersten 1994 (via Schlunssen-2018). Milicia regia not separately checked.
